get.description: List connected WhatsApp (and Green-API) phone numbers for the authenticated business. Call this before creating a workflow: if more than one number is returned, ask the user which one to bind. Copy the chosen row's `id` into the workflow `associatedToBusinessId` (not `associatedBusinessId`, which is the WABA id) and set `platformType`. For a starter/outbound bot (or a named catalog template), pass the same `id` as `phoneNumberId` on GET `/templates`. Skip GET `/templates` for inbound reply bots (`pingmeeTrigger`) unless the user named a template. Facebook pages and Instagram accounts are not in this list. See `/build-workflows/document` (platform binding) and `/build-workflows/overview`.

phoneNumbers.description: Connected WhatsApp / Green-API numbers. Use `id` as workflow `associatedToBusinessId`.

id.description: Phone-number id. Copy this into workflow `associatedToBusinessId` and into GET `/templates?phoneNumberId=`.

associatedBusinessId.description: WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) id. Do not put this in `associatedToBusinessId`.

mcp.name: get-phone-numbers
mcp.description: List connected WhatsApp phone numbers. Ask the user which number to bind, then set workflow associatedToBusinessId to the row id (not associatedBusinessId / WABA). Use that id as phoneNumberId on GET /templates only for starter/outbound bots or a named catalog template — not for inbound reply bots.

get.description: List WhatsApp message templates for a connected phone number (`type=whatsapp` and `phoneNumberId` required). `phoneNumberId` is the workflow `associatedToBusinessId` (GET `/phone-numbers` row `id`). Call this for **starter/outbound** bots (`workflowTrigger`, POST `/workflows/{id}/trigger`, campaign-style send, or any send outside the 24-hour window), or when the user named a catalog template. Do **not** call this for inbound reply bots (`pingmeeTrigger` `Messages Created` / `New Conversation Started`) — those use `messageType: custom`. When you do fetch: pick an APPROVED template, copy it into the WhatsApp node's `templateInformation`, set `messageType: template` and `templateType: whatsapp`, and bind `bodyVariables` / `headerVariables`. Skip IMAGE / VIDEO / DOCUMENT header templates unless `attachmentS3Id` is already on the component — there is no public upload API. Infer intent: `/build-workflows/overview`. Field mapping: `/build-workflows/nodes-and-edges`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Template platform type. Use `whatsapp` for Meta catalog templates.

parameters.name: phoneNumberId
parameters.description: Phone-number id from GET `/phone-numbers` (workflow `associatedToBusinessId`). Do not use the WABA id.

name.description: Template name. Copy into `templateInformation.name`. Do not invent this.

status.description: Use only `APPROVED` templates when the bot opens a conversation (starter/outbound). Reply bots do not need this list.

components.description: HEADER / BODY / FOOTER / BUTTONS. Copy the array into `templateInformation.components`. Bind BODY `{{n}}` with `bodyVariables` and text HEADER `{{n}}` with `headerVariables`.

mcp.name: get-templates
mcp.description: Get WhatsApp templates for a phone number (workflow associatedToBusinessId). Call only for starter/outbound bots or a named catalog template — not for inbound reply bots (pingmeeTrigger). When opening a conversation: copy APPROVED into templateInformation, set messageType template and templateType whatsapp, bind bodyVariables / headerVariables. No public media upload.

post.description:
Create a workflow. Client supplies `workflowId` in the path (URL-encode it). Required query: `folderId`. Body requires `name`. Before saving, GET `/phone-numbers`, ask the user which number to bind, and set `associatedToBusinessId` to that row's `id` plus `platformType`. Infer intent: if the bot **opens** a WhatsApp conversation (starter/outbound, `workflowTrigger`, POST `/trigger`), GET `/templates` and use an APPROVED template on the first WhatsApp node; inbound reply bots (`pingmeeTrigger`) use `messageType: custom` and should not fetch templates unless the user named one. Graph fields (`data`, `parsedData`, `trigger`, `triggerType`, `variables`) are optional — you can send a full document. The server overwrites `id`, `associatedTo` (from the Cookie), `folderId`, `isActive` (always `false`), `created`, `lastModified`, `executionCount`, `lastExecution`, and `analytics`. Returns `{ message, created, lastModified }`.

Before building `data` / `parsedData`, read `/build-workflows/overview` and the related Build workflows cookbook pages. Recommended save sequence: optional POST `/folders/{id}` → POST this endpoint (name + phone ids + optional graph) → PUT `{ isActive: true }`. Graph PUTs must echo `lastModified`.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Client-supplied workflow identifier. Must be URL-encoded when used in the path.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: Folder to place the workflow in. Create a folder with POST `/folders/{id}` or reuse `folderId` from the minimal list.

requestBody.description: At least `name`. Optionally include the full dual graph (`data`, `parsedData`, `trigger`, `triggerType`, `variables`) and other Workflow fields. `isActive` in the body is ignored — the server always stores `false`.

associatedToBusinessId.description: WhatsApp phone-number id from GET `/phone-numbers` (row `id`, not `associatedBusinessId` / WABA). Required for WhatsApp send. Ask the user if more than one number exists.

associatedToPlatformId.description: Optional alias of the same phone-number / page id as `associatedToBusinessId`.

platformType.description: `whatsapp`, `facebookMessenger`, `instagram`, or `web`. Set on create together with `associatedToBusinessId`.

variables.description: Workflow-level variable map. Usually `{}` unless set.

parsedData.description: Execution graph: parent nodes only. Sub-nodes hang off `parent.subNodes[]`.

lastModified.description: Unix timestamp (seconds). Echo this on later graph PUTs.

mcp.name: post-workflows-workflowId
mcp.description: Create a workflow. Client supplies workflowId in the path (URL-encode it). Required query folderId. Body requires name. Fetch GET /phone-numbers first and set associatedToBusinessId to the chosen row id plus platformType. Infer intent: starter/outbound bots GET /templates and use an APPROVED WhatsApp template; inbound reply bots (pingmeeTrigger) use messageType custom and skip templates unless the user named one. Graph fields (data, parsedData, trigger, triggerType, variables) are optional; you can send a full document. Server forces isActive false and sets associatedTo from the Cookie. Returns { message, created, lastModified }. Before building data / parsedData, read /build-workflows/overview. Recommended save sequence: optional POST /folders/{id} → POST this endpoint (name + phone ids + optional graph) → PUT { isActive: true }. Graph PUTs must echo lastModified.

put.description:
Update a workflow. `name`, `isActive`, `settings`, and `associatedToBusinessId` can be sent alone — including `{ isActive: true }` to activate without sending a graph. If `data` or `parsedData` is present, this is a graph update: also send `trigger`, `triggerType`, `variables`, and `lastModified` from the last GET or create, or the API returns 409. Always send both `data` and `parsedData` plus `trigger` / `triggerType` on graph save. Do not send `analytics`. A graph PUT prunes stored analytics for node, edge, and button ids that are no longer on the graph — GET fresh analytics before rewriting.

Before building `data` / `parsedData`, read `/build-workflows/overview` and `/build-workflows/analytics`. Path `workflowId` must be URL-encoded.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Workflow identifier. Must be URL-encoded when used in the path.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Send only the fields you want to change. Graph updates (`data` or `parsedData` present) require `lastModified` from the last GET or create.

isActive.description: Set `true` to activate. Create always stores `false`; activate with a separate PUT `{ isActive: true }` (no graph required).

lastModified.description: Required when `data` or `parsedData` is present. Echo the value from the last GET or create, or the API returns 409.

associatedToBusinessId.description: WhatsApp phone-number id from GET `/phone-numbers` (row `id`). PUT can change this field without sending a graph.

lastModified.description: New Unix timestamp (seconds). Echo this on the next graph PUT.

409.description: Optimistic lock conflict — workflow was updated elsewhere. Reload with GET and retry using the returned `lastModified`.

message.example: Workflow was updated elsewhere. Reload and try again.

mcp.name: put-workflows-workflowId
mcp.description: Update a workflow. name, isActive, settings, and associatedToBusinessId can be sent alone — including { isActive: true } to activate without sending a graph. If data or parsedData is present, send trigger, triggerType, variables, and lastModified from the last GET or create, or the API returns 409. Do not send analytics. A graph PUT prunes stored analytics for removed node, edge, and button ids. Path workflowId must be URL-encoded.

post.description: Manually trigger a bot workflow for a conversation. This call is a **starter**: it opens the thread from the business side, so the workflow's first WhatsApp node must be `messageType: template` + `templateType: whatsapp` with an APPROVED catalog template. Optional body `triggerData` is copied onto the trigger node output and read with `return $<triggerNodeId>.triggerData.<key>;`. Path `workflowId` must be URL-encoded.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Workflow identifier. Must be URL-encoded when used in the path.

requestBody.description: Conversation, optional node to start from, and optional `triggerData` JSON copied onto the trigger node output.

triggerData.description: Optional JSON object copied onto the trigger node's output as `triggerData`. Downstream expressions read it as `return $<triggerNodeId>.triggerData.<key>;` (the `$…` id is the trigger node id, not the workflow id). Must be a JSON object (not an array), at most 32768 bytes, nesting depth at most 10. See Build workflows → Variables.

startWithNodeId.description: Optional workflow node identifier to start execution from.

mcp.name: post-workflows-workflowId-trigger
mcp.description: Manually trigger a bot workflow for a conversation (starter/outbound). First WhatsApp node must be messageType template + templateType whatsapp. Optional body triggerData is copied onto the trigger node output and read with return $<triggerNodeId>.triggerData.<key>;. Path workflowId must be URL-encoded.

post.description: Zeros every canvas analytics counter on this workflow (`totalStarted`, `totalCompleted`, `totalDropped`, `nodeStats`, `edgeStats`, `buttonStats`). No request body. Requires the Expert AI plan (`403` otherwise). Destructive — call only when the user explicitly asks. Returns the updated workflow document. Use the new `lastModified` on the next graph PUT. Path `workflowId` must be URL-encoded. Same Cookie + `x-api-key` as other Workflows calls. See `/build-workflows/analytics`.

parameters.description: Workflow identifier. Must be URL-encoded when used in the path.

statusCase.description: Task status. Built-in values are `open`, `standby` (in progress), and `completed`. Custom task status IDs defined for the business are also accepted.

unreadCount.description: Needs-attention counter. Starts at 1 on create and increments on every update.

assignedAgentIds.description: Agent IDs assigned to this task.

viewedByAgentIds.description: Agent IDs that have viewed this task.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the task was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the task was last updated.

dueDate.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) for the due date. `0` when unset.

phoneNumberId.description: Business phone number identifier used to scope the task.

participantsIdentifiers.description: Conversation participants identifiers this task is linked to.

UpdateTask.description: Partial task update. Include only the fields you want to change. `unreadCount`, `updatedAt`, and `agentIdentification` are set by the server.

statusCase.description: Task status. Built-in values are `open`, `standby` (in progress), and `completed`. Custom task status IDs defined for the business are also accepted.

assignedAgentIds.description: Agent IDs assigned to this task. Replaces the full assignment list.

viewedByAgentIds.description: Agent IDs that have viewed this task.

dueDate.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) for the due date. `0` to unset.

participantsIdentifiers.description: Conversation participants identifiers this task is linked to.

phoneNumberId.description: Business phone number identifier used to scope the task.

associatedTo.description: Business or account the conversation is associated with.

participantsIdentifiers.description: Unique identifiers of the conversation participants.

lastMessage.description: Last message exchanged in the conversation.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when the conversation was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when the conversation was last updated.

unreadCount.description: Number of unread messages in the conversation.

assignedTagIds.description: List of assigned conversation tag IDs.

lastWorkflowExecutionId.description: Identifier of the last workflow execution.

lastSendMessageFromUser.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) of the last message sent by the user.

isOptoutFromMarketingMessages.description: Indicates whether the customer opted out of marketing messages.

WhatsAppMessageContext.description: Reply context for a WhatsApp message

AITranslation.description: AI translation payload for the message

WhatsAppErrorMessage.description: WhatsApp / platform error details when sending failed

AgentIdentification.description: Agent who sent or handled the message

Message.description: A prepared message returned by getMessages

initiator.description: Who initiated the message (`Initiator`, e.g. person, bot, ai)

messagePlatform.description: Platform the message was sent on (`PlatformType`)

creationPlatform.description: Platform where the message was created (`PlatformType`)

informativeMessageType.description: System / informative message subtype when applicable (`InformativeMessageType`)

MessagesCursorKey.description: Pagination cursor. Returned as `lastEvaluatedKey` in the response; send the same object as `startKey` on the next request to load the next batch. Shape: `{ "messageId": "<string>", "createdAt": <number> }` (Unix milliseconds). Omit `startKey` on the first request.

messageId.description: Message ID from the pagination cursor (`lastEvaluatedKey`)

GetMessagesRequest.description: Use `startKey` only after the first page: set it to `lastEvaluatedKey` from the prior response to fetch the next batch.

dbObject.description: Messages (newest first), each a prepared `Message` object

hasMoreItemsToFetch.description: Whether more messages exist beyond this page

lastEvaluatedKey.description: When present, use this value as `startKey` in the next request to fetch the next batch of (older) messages.

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to assign (POST) or remove (DELETE) from the conversation

errors.description: Human-readable messages for tags that failed to remove; empty when all succeeded

WorkflowNodeStats.description: Per-node canvas counters. Keyed by node or sub-node id in `analytics.nodeStats`.

exitedCount.description: Times execution left this node via an outgoing edge (or a button click on a parent).

WorkflowEdgeStats.description: Per-edge traversal counters. Map key is `{sourceNodeId}->{targetNodeId}` or `{sourceNodeId}->{targetNodeId}:{sourceHandle}`.

sourceHandle.description: Root outgoing edges use `out`. Sub-node outgoing edges (answers, If true/false, switch cases) use `in`. Older runs may store the sub-node id instead of `in`.

WorkflowButtonStats.description: WhatsApp answer sub-node clicks. Map key is the answer `subNodeId`, not the parent message id.

label.description: Button label as recorded at click time.

payload.description: Optional button payload recorded at click time.

WorkflowAnalytics.description: Canvas analytics on GET `/workflows/{workflowId}` (Expert AI plan). Omitted when the plan does not include canvas analytics — do not invent counts. Server-managed; do not send on PUT. A graph PUT prunes `nodeStats`, `edgeStats`, and `buttonStats` for ids no longer on the graph. See `/build-workflows/analytics`.

totalDropped.description: Executions that ended in failure or expiry (not success).

lastUpdated.description: Optional. Epoch milliseconds of the last recorded analytics event.

nodeStats.description: Per-node counters keyed by node or sub-node id.

buttonStats.description: Answer-button clicks keyed by answer sub-node id. If/Else and switch paths are node+edge stats on the branch sub-node, not buttonStats.

associatedTo.description: Account id. Set by the server from the Cookie — do not invent this value.

associatedToBusinessId.description: WhatsApp phone-number id from GET `/phone-numbers` (row `id`, not the WABA `associatedBusinessId`) or Facebook page id. Required for WhatsApp send. See `/build-workflows/document`.

associatedToPlatformId.description: Optional alias of the same phone-number id or Facebook page id as `associatedToBusinessId`.

platformType.description: Platform this workflow is bound to (`whatsapp`, `facebookMessenger`, `instagram`, `web`). Set on create with `associatedToBusinessId`.

isActive.description: Whether the workflow runs. Create always stores `false`. Activate with PUT `{ isActive: true }`.

created.description: Unix timestamp (seconds). Set by the server on create.

lastModified.description: Unix timestamp (seconds). Echo this on graph PUTs or the API returns 409.

triggerType.description: Usually `trigger.data.eventType`. The trigger node is `workflow.trigger`, not inside `parsedData`.

variables.description: Workflow-level variable map. Usually `{}` unless set. Nested variable objects are loose — see `/build-workflows/variables`.

parsedData.description: Execution graph: parent nodes only. Sub-nodes hang off `parent.subNodes[]`. Runtime starts at `trigger.connections.out[0]`.

settings.description: Optional shared timeout / fallback and other workflow settings.

executionCount.description: Number of times the workflow has executed. Server-managed.

lastExecution.description: Unix timestamp of the last execution. Server-managed.

selected.description: Editor UI flag. Not required for API saves.

WorkflowCanvas.description: React Flow canvas (`workflow.data` from `toObject()`). Required for the editor. Always send together with `parsedData` + `trigger` when saving a graph. Node form payloads are not fully specified here — read `/build-workflows/overview` before building `data`.

nodes.description: Canvas nodes. Sub-nodes are siblings in this array (they have `parentId`), not nested.

parentId.description: Set on sub-nodes. Sub-nodes are siblings in `data.nodes`, not nested.

data.description: Node form payload. Shape depends on `type` — see `/build-workflows/overview`. Do not invent every field from this schema.

WorkflowEdge.description: React Flow edge. Copy every edge into execution `connections.out` with matching node ids (see `/build-workflows/canvas-vs-execution`). Root node output handle is `out`; input is `in`. Sub-node output handle is also `in` (downstream edges from a branch use `sourceHandle: "in"`). Type is usually `buttonedge`.

source.description: Source node id. Must match a `data.nodes[].id`.

target.description: Target node id. Must match a `data.nodes[].id`.

sourceHandle.description: Root output is `out`. Sub-node output is `in`.

WorkflowNode.description: Execution node used in `parsedData`, `trigger`, and `subNodes`. Branching is which sub-node's `connections.out` — there are no handle ids here. Node `data` is a loose object; read `/build-workflows/overview` before building it.

parentId.description: Parent node id when this node is a sub-node.

title.description: Used by the engine for some branches (If/Else matches `title.toLowerCase()` of `true` / `false`).

data.description: Node form payload. Shape depends on `type` — see `/build-workflows/overview`.

connections.description: Typically `{ out: string[] }` of target node ids. No handle ids.

subNodes.description: Child branch nodes (answers, true/false, switch cases, fallback, timeout). Not used on canvas `data.nodes` — those are siblings with `parentId`.

name.description: Role name (max 40 characters). Also used to derive the OpenAI function tool name.

description.description: Short description of the role (max 1500 characters)

instructions.description: Instructions used when generating the role tool schema (max 1500 characters)

webhook.description: Webhook URL invoked when this role tool is called (max 300 characters)

allRequired.description: When true, generated tool parameters are all required (strict mode)

required.description: Whether the agent must use the vector store for answers

files.description: Files currently in the vector store

fileNamesMapping.description: Map of vector store file IDs to display names

description.description: Business / agent description used as context (max 5000 characters)

created.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when the agent was created

lastModified.description: Unix timestamp (milliseconds) when the agent was last modified

tokensUsed.description: Cumulative tokens used by this agent

UpdateAIAgent.description: Partial update payload for an AI agent. Length limits: description 5000; role name 40; role description/instructions 1500; role webhook 300.

roles.description: Full roles list. Changed roles regenerate their tool schemas. Limits: name 40, description 1500, instructions 1500, webhook 300.

required.description: Whether the agent must use the vector store

agents.description: Flat list of AI agents for this page

lastEvaluatedKey.description: Pagination cursor for the next page. Pass URI-encoded as `exclusiveStartKey`.

WebhookEvent.description: Event type the webhook is subscribed to.

color.description: Status color (hex, rgb, or named color)

associatedTo.description: Business or account the status is associated with

isSelected.description: Whether this status is selected in the UI

id.description: Unique identifier of the status. Can be used as a task `statusCase`.

associatedTo.description: Business or account the status is associated with

isSelected.description: Whether this status is selected in the UI

title.description: Human-readable status title. Must be unique for the business.

color.description: Status color (hex, rgb, or named color)

cookieAuth.name: Cookie
cookieAuth.description: Personal access token from Pingmee Settings → Developer Tools

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Business API key from Pingmee Settings → Developer Tools
